tool.name: RRules Parser
tool.description: Download and filter RetroRules releases or local reaction rules
tool.command: python -m rrparser #if str($rules.source) == 'retrorules': --rules_file retrorules --cache-dir './rrparser-cache' --release '$rules.release.kind' #if str($rules.release.kind) == 'rr02': --dataset metanetx --rule-type '$rules.release.rule_type' #else: --dataset '$rules.release.dataset' --rule-type all #end if #else: --rules_file '$rules.file' --input-format '$rules.input_format' #if str($rules.input_schema.kind) == 'legacy': --rule-type '$rules.input_schema.rule_type' #else: --rule-type all #end if #end if #if str($adv.size.mode) == 'list': --radii '$adv.size.radii' #else: --radii '$adv.size.expression' #end if #if str($adv.ec.mode) == 'in': --ec '$adv.ec.file' #elif str($adv.ec.mode) == 'out': --ecx '$adv.ec.file' #end if #if $adv.scores: --scores '$adv.scores' #end if --output-format csv #if $adv.compress: --outfile './rules.csv.gz' && mv './rules.csv.gz' '$out_rules' #else: --outfile '$out_rules' #end if

tool.help:
RRules Parser =============
Download RetroRules datasets or filter a CSV/TSV rules file from your history. Choose the rules source directly. Every run produces a CSV dataset in your Galaxy history, ready to inspect, use in another tool, or download.
Rules source ------------
**Download from RetroRules** offers three releases:
* **Latest available release** (default): selects the newest template release compatible with all selected datasets. It is not permanently tied to 3.1.0. * **RetroRules 3.0**: selects the explicit release identifier ``3.0``. * **RetroRules rr02 — historical rules**: selects legacy RetroPath 2.0 rules.
For Latest and 3.0, the **Datasets** list allows selecting one or more of **MetaNetX**, **Rhea**, and **USPTO**. Select all three to combine them all. Selected datasets are merged within one release; versions are never mixed. With Latest, the package selects the newest release containing every requested dataset. Templates automatically use rule usage **All**.
Historical rr02 supports **MetaNetX only** and exposes **All**, **Retro**, and **Forward** usage filters. It does not display a dataset selector.
Downloading requires network access from the Galaxy execution host. Source archives are cached in the job working directory, without a shared cache between jobs. Select 3.0 rather than Latest for a fixed release.
**Rules file from history** accepts a local CSV or TSV file. Select its input format and schema. Legacy rules contain ``Diameter`` and ``Rule usage`` columns and support All/Retro/Forward. Templates contain ``TEMPLATE_ID`` and ``RADII`` and automatically use All. Release and dataset selectors do not apply to files from history.
Advanced Options ----------------
Choose a list of radius values or a radius expression. Valid radii are the integers 0–10, all selected by default. Expressions support inclusive ranges, comparisons, and unions, for example ``0-8``, ``>8``, ``>=8``, or ``0-4,9,10``. Ranges include odd and even radii. Lower bounds must not exceed upper bounds.
Lists and expressions are passed directly through ``--radii``. RRParser 2.7.3 expands them into normalized integer radii before parsing the rules. For example, ``>8`` selects radii 9/10, and ``>=8`` includes radius 8 as well. The wrapper does not pass ``--diameters`` and does not use an external conversion helper.
A template is retained when at least one of its source radii matches. Its RADII column keeps all original radii, so a row marked ``8;9`` is retained by ``>8``.
rr02 supplies diameters 2–16, equivalent to radii 1–8. Radius ``>8`` therefore produces a header-only output for rr02. Empty selections such as ``>10`` also produce a header-only CSV. The form restricts individual values and expression bounds to 0–10.
EC filtering keeps or removes matching prefixes from a text file containing one comma-separated line, for example ``1.1,2.7``. Inclusion and exclusion are mutually exclusive.
An optional replacement scores file must contain ``Rule ID`` and ``Score`` columns. Use CSV for downloaded rules, or the same delimiter as a local input. EC filtering and score replacement apply after dataset merging.
Enable **Compress output with gzip** to save the output as a gzip-compressed CSV dataset. Leave it unchecked to obtain an uncompressed CSV.
Output and compatibility ------------------------
The extracted rules are saved automatically in your Galaxy history: CSV by default, or gzip-compressed CSV when compression is enabled. Compressed output uses the Galaxy datatype **gz** and contains a CSV file. No output filename is required. Download the dataset from its history panel if you want a local copy.
Template outputs rename ``TEMPLATE_ID``, ``TEMPLATE``, ``ECS``, and ``SCORE`` to ``Rule ID``, ``Rule``, ``EC number``, and ``Score``. Other source columns are retained. Their schema and implicit hydrogen SMARTS differ from rr02's explicit hydrogen RetroPath 2.0 rules. Use rr02 when downstream tools require the historical format.
Review older saved workflows when upgrading: the conditional parameter layout has changed.
